item.title: U.S.-Iran war widens further after drone strikes on Egyptian port
item.description: U.S. Central Command released new video it said to show fighter jets launching what it described as a "heavy wave" of strikes against Iran. It was the first resumption of strikes in several days. The U.S. said it was in direct retaliation for the recent missile attack on U.S. forces in Jordan. Charlie D'Agata reports.

item.title: Trump says he may pull Blanche's nomination until 2 Senate critics leave office
item.description: President Trump said Todd Blanche will remain acting attorney general as a holdup on his nomination continues.

item.title: ICE agents increasingly arresting immigrants at U.S. airports
item.description: ICE agents have ramped up arrests at some U.S. airports, working with the TSA to crack down on travelers at check-in counters and even at the departure gates. Camilo Montoya-Galvez has the story.

item.title: El-Sayed leading Stevens in Michigan Democratic primary for Senate, poll finds
item.description: A new Emerson College poll shows Dr. Abdul El-Sayed leading Rep. Haley Stevens in Michigan's Democratic primary for a U.S. Senate seat. CBS News' Fin Gomez has more on that race and some of the other 2026 midterm battles.

item.title: Spain deploys military to Morocco border after migrant crossings, 9 deaths
item.description: Spain will deploy its military to Ceuta to help restore order at its border with Morocco after local authorities in Ceuta had asked the central government in Madrid for reinforcements.

item.title: Trump suggests he may pause Blanche's confirmation amid GOP pushback
item.description: Attorney General nominee Todd Blanche's confirmation is on hold after some Republican senators refused to vote for him. President Trump suggested that he may press pause on the nomination. Nikole Killion has more details.

item.title: CBS News poll: Many Americans don't see inflation relief coming from either side of political aisle
item.description: As the perceived disparity between incomes and inflation continues to grow, new CBS News polling shows many Americans don't feel relief coming from Republicans or Democrats. CBS News executive director of elections and surveys Anthony Salvanto breaks down the findings.

item.title: Police fatally shoot suspect in deadly California kidnapping
item.description: On Wednesday night in Chino Hills, about 30 miles south of Los Angeles, deputies fatally shot a suspect after a deadly kidnapping. Carter Evans reports as authorities piece together exactly what happened.

item.title: Massive explosion rocks quiet Ohio neighborhood
item.description: A massive explosion rocked a quiet Ohio neighborhood on Thursday. The blast was caught on video. Tom Hanson has the details.

item.title: Retired Navy vice admiral says it would be "quite an escalation" if Egypt were to join Iran war
item.description: The Iran war appears to have expanded to Egypt after drone strikes sparked fires in the country. Who conducted the strikes remains unknown. Ret. Navy Vice Adm. Robert Murrett joins with analysis.

item.title: Lindsay Clancy triple murder scene "turned very chaotic, very quickly," paramedic testifies
item.description: Lindsay Clancy is facing three first-degree murder charges, accused of killing her children in her Duxbury, Massachusetts, home in 2023. Thursday was the third day of witness testimony.

item.title: Thousands of migrants stream into Spain from Morocco, authorities report 9 dead
item.description: Thousands of migrants streamed into the Spanish city of Ceuta on foot and by sea from Morocco on Thursday, as federal troops helped overwhelmed police. Several migrants were reported dead. Matt Gutman reports.

item.title: Stolen Civil War-era cannonballs found in suitcase at Alabama airport
item.description: Law enforcement officials say a set of stolen Civil War-era cannonballs was discovered in a passenger's suitcase during a routine security screening at Alabama's Gulf Shores International Airport.

item.title: Hair sample found at Nancy Guthrie's home inconclusive as search hits 6-month mark
item.description: A hair sample found at the home of Nancy Guthrie came back inconclusive after undergoing testing, Pima County Sheriff Chris Nanos revealed Thursday.

item.title: French wildfires threatening wine production in Bordeaux
item.description: Much of Europe is still dealing with heat and high winds that are fueling major wildfires. Those fires are threatening France's world famous wine region.y. CBS News' Ramy Inocencio reports and Ray Isle, executive wine editor at Food & Wine, joins "The Daily Report" to discuss the impact of the wildfires on the wine industry.

item.title: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman expresses support for AI development slowdown
item.description: Emily Birnbaum, a corporate lobbying reporter at Bloomberg News, joins "The Daily Report" to discuss what OpenAI CEO Sam Altman's lobbying efforts in Washington, D.C., mean for the industry as he voices his support for pacing AI development.

item.title: Trump says he might pull Todd Blanche's AG nomination until Cornyn and Tillis leave office
item.description: President Trump on Thursday threatened to temporarily pull Todd Blanche's nomination for attorney general amid opposition from Republican Senators John Cornyn and Thom Tillis. CBS News' Taurean Small has the details.

item.title: Democratic, Republican strategists unpack stalled Blanche nomination, Michigan Senate race and more
item.description: President Trump on Thursday said he may pull his nomination of Todd Blanche for attorney general until GOP Sens. John Cornyn and Thom Tillis leave office. Political strategists Usamah Andrabi and Kevin Sheridan join "The Takeout" with analysis.

item.title: Latest on Iran war as conflict appears to expand in Middle East
item.description: The war in Iran appears to be expanding after drone strikes at Egypt's Mediterranean port of Damietta sparked fires on two natural gas vessels Wednesday. CBS News' chief White House correspondent Nancy Cordes has more.

item.title: Rep. Max Miller facing domestic abuse allegations as he runs for reelection
item.description: Republican Rep. Max Miller of Ohio is facing allegations of domestic abuse, which he denies. Nikki McCann Ramirez, co-author of a Rolling Stone article published this week on the accusations and the GOP response, joins "The Takeout" with more.

item.title: New forecast shifts 13 House seats, Georgia Senate race toward Democrats
item.description: The University of Virginia's election forecaster Sabato's Crystal Ball has updated its outlook for this year's midterm elections, favoring Democrats in some House races and the Georgia Senate race. Sabato's managing editor, Kyle Kondik, joins "The Takeout" to discuss.

item.title: Rep. Ralph Norman says he expects South Carolina GOP Senate primary to go to runoff amid tight polls
item.description: A new poll from Emerson College shows a tight race to fill the late Lindsey Graham's Senate seat. Rep. Ralph Norman, who the poll showed with a slim lead over Graham's sister, Darline, joins "The Takeout" to discuss his campaign.

item.title: CONCACAF rejects Infantino's World Cup investment plan after UEFA's boycott threat
item.description: North America's soccer body on Thursday rejected FIFA president Gianni Infantino's plan to sell stakes in the World Cup to private equity investors, joining European nations in opposition.

item.title: Battle against monster wildfire in France boosted by improving weather
item.description: George and Amal Clooney are among thousands of residents in southwest France still displaced by a massive wildfire, but crews are gaining control.

item.title: The Texas Yogurt Shop Exonerations | Case by Case
item.description: For decades, Maurice Pierce, Robert Springsteen, Michael Scott and Forrest Welborn lived under the shadow of the yogurt shop murders, a crime that left an indelible mark on Austin and forever changed the lives of the the families of the victims: Eliza Thomas, Amy Ayers, and sisters Jennifer and Sarah Harbison. All four men were ultimately declared innocent and later exonerated after investigators linked another man to the killings. After reporting on this case for more 30 years, "48 Hours" correspondent Erin Moriarty speaks with Pierce's widow and daughter about the devastating toll of a wrongful accusation, their family's fight to clear his name, a financial settlement, and what justice means when it arrives decades too late.

item.title: Survivor Finalist Joe Hunter's Fight for Justice | Case by Case
item.description: During his time competing on "Survivor," Joe Hunter has been open about seeking justice for the death of his sister Joanna whose death was ruled a suicide. "48 Hours" correspondent Natalie Morales and producer Michelle Fanucci discuss their investigation into Joanna's death and an interview with Hunter who believes Joanna's husband, former pastor Mark Lewis, staged the scene after years of domestic violence. Mark Lewis has not been charged with any crime relating to the death of Joanna.

item.title: The Trial of Larry Millete Begins | Case by Case
item.description: After years of waiting, Larry Millete's murder trial is underway in San Diego. He is accused of killing his wife, Maya Millete, who disappeared in 2021. The first week has already delivered bombshell testimony. In this episode of "Case by Case," "48 Hours" correspondent Anne-Marie Green and CBS 8 San Diego reporter Kelly Hessedal break down the 2021 disappearance of Maya before diving into the stunning allegations laid out in court – including an alleged affair and emails with online spellcasters.

item.title: How a County Clerk Upended the Alex Murdaugh Case | Case by Case
item.description: The South Carolina Supreme Court just issued a stunning unanimous ruling overturning the 2023 double murder convictions of Alex Murdaugh. In this episode of "Case by Case," "48 Hours" correspondent Anne-Marie Green and University of South Carolina School of Law professor Colin Miller break down the jury tampering allegations against Becky Hill that sent this notorious case back to square one.

item.title: Consulting AI for Murder | Case by Case
item.description: Last week, the remains of the second victim in the slaying of two University of South Florida students were finally identified. Zamil Limon and Nahida Bristy were both doctoral candidates from Bangladesh. Hisham Abugharbieh, Limon's roommate, has been charged with two counts of first-degree murder in connection to their deaths. On this episode of "Case by Case," "48 Hours" correspondent Natalie Morales and Miami-based CBS News correspondent Cristian Benavides break down what we know so far, and how, according to prosecutors, the suspected killer consulted AI to help plan the crimes. Limon and Bristy will both receive posthumous degrees on Friday.

item.title: Deadly Vacations | Case by Case
item.description: Why are so many dream vacations turning into true crime headlines? On the premiere episode of "Case by Case," we examine the trial of Gerhardt Konig, the former anesthesiologist found guilty of attempted manslaughter after a brutal cliffside attack on his wife Arielle in Hawaii. "48 Hours" correspondent Natalie Morales and CBS News chief correspondent Matt Gutman break down the trial's most stunning moments before diving into the chilling trend of headlines about vacations that turned deadly. From the ridges of Oahu to the waters of the Bahamas, we'll follow it all, "Case by Case."
